topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture's scope and states what students should understand by its end.

topics.label: Mutational and epigenetic drivers of tumor development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cellular alterations drive tumor development, extending the mutation-based account of clonal evolution to changes in transcriptional state.

topics.label: Stemness, cancer stem cells and the cell of origin
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate how a cell's position in a tissue hierarchy affects its capacity to initiate and sustain tumor growth.

topics.label: Inflammation-induced stemness and cancer initiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how inflammatory signals can confer stem-like properties that enable mutation-bearing cells to develop into tumors.

topics.label: Microenvironmental support of established tumors
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines established tumors' dependence on supportive surrounding cells and the therapeutic opportunities created by that dependence.

topics.label: Methods for studying cancer evolution and cell interactions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how molecular and spatial measurements of tissue reveal tumor evolution and interactions between cell populations.

topics.label: An integrated account of cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This synthesis explains malignant outgrowth as the convergence of cellular fitness and a permissive environment, extending that account to susceptibility at different stages of life.

topics.label: Lecture close and next lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This closing ends the lecture and announces the forthcoming discussion of therapy.
